correctness.rationale: Every quantifier and boundary is covered: n>=3, t>0, nonnegative priced conductances on a connected wheel, and real s in the critical scaling. Strict convexity plus injective edge-to-Laplacian map makes the symmetric solution the sole global minimum. Fourier decomposition gives its exact eigenvalues, F_n is strictly convex, and the sign F_n'(0)=n^2 t/(n+1)-2n proves the finite cutoff. The Riemann-sum limiting objective and endpoint exclusion prove the fixed-price phase law; the two exact cycle moments and local Hessian prove the critical window. A separate exact-Fraction checker passed 196 finite algebra/derivative instances. Finite cases are corroboration, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The closest established source [Ghosh–Boyd–Saberi 2008, sec. 5.2] gives the equal-price wheel spectrum, implicit unpriced optimum and convex framework. The claimed all-price deletion threshold 2(n+1)/n and the explicit macroscopic/critical-window price law are not in its wheel theorem and are not implied by the single t=1 case. Bapat–Gupta computes wheel resistances, not the stated price-budget optimum. A directly relevant 2008 weighted-wheel index paper was only bibliographically accessible; risk is recorded rather than assumed absent. Searches against a published-results semantic index and primary sources found no exact/stronger statement. The assessment does not claim completeness of literature discovery.

value.rationale: The budgeted wheel is a natural two-class network design family with a real link-installation decision. The threshold 2(n+1)/n exactly decides when all rim conductance is optimally zero for every size, and the sharp price-two limit yields nonzero optimal rim/spoke budget shares, an exact efficiency gain, and an n-dependent finite-size transition with a calculable leading benefit. This is a structurally motivated all-dimensional result, not a small arbitrary numerical adjustment or normalization check.
